correctness.rationale: The rook graph is L(K_m,n); selected cells induce a graph with cycles precisely when selected bipartite edges have degree>=3 (a line-graph triangle) or contain a cycle, hence induced forests correspond bijectively to bipartite linear forests including isolated base vertices. Two-sorted labeled exponential formula on alternating paths with r/r and r+1/r vertex counts gives exp(u+v+[uv z+uv(u+v)z²/2]/[1-uvz²]); reversals and factorial normalizations are correctly counted. Inclusion-maximal selected linear forest iff every pair of selected-degree<=1 vertices on opposite sides lies in one component. If both sides have low-degree vertices, this forces one spanning path with opposite-side endpoints, thus m=n and size m+n-1. For m<n, every vertex of smaller side has degree2 (the opposite alternative violates forest edge bound), giving size 2m; after contracting degree2 small-side vertices the larger side carries a simple linear forest with m edges and n-m components, whose path EGF B(u)=u+u²/[2(1-u)] and m! distinct edge labels give m!n!/(n-m)! [u^n]B(u)^{n-m}. m=n gives (m!)² alternating Hamilton paths. Small cases and empty/isolated vertices are accounted for. Independent union-find cycle tests on actual rook-cell induced subgraphs, not the repository checker, reconstructed entire polynomial and maximal counts for (2,2),(2,3),(2,4),(3,3),(3,4); finite enumeration is corroboration only.
residual_risks: The theorem concerns vertex-induced forests of LINE graph L(K_m,n), not base graph vertex forests or independent rooks.
The EGF includes m=0/n=0 for formal identity, while purity theorem quantifies m,n>=2; all counts for labeled row/column vertices.

value.rationale: The theorem supplies a complete face enumerator and facet enumerator of a natural two-parameter induced-forest simplicial complex, plus unexpected purity. The sharp transition from alternating Hamilton paths (m=n) to contracted linear forests (m<n) is a structural classification beyond largest-set size. The exact labeled coefficient formula is a natural reusable invariant for later topological/combinatorial study, not an arbitrary slice.
residual_risks: No claim of purity for arbitrary line graphs or Cartesian products; arbitrary other forest-graph invariants remain open.

limitations: m,n>=2 for purity; all-size EGF extends formally to zero rows/columns.
